You are auditing the marketing website of the Nxeon VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Tailwind v4, TypeScript) ahead of a complete front-end redesign. This is READ-ONLY analysis — do NOT edit, build, or commit anything. Produce a precise inventory and diagnosis.

Scope of the marketing/public site (do NOT audit the customer dashboard or admin portal):
- app/page.tsx (homepage)
- app/(marketing)/* — features, pricing, vps, domains, game-servers, compare, vps-vs-digitalocean, vps-vs-hostinger, about, contact, and app/(marketing)/layout.tsx
- app/blog/*, app/status/page.tsx, app/legal/*
- components/marketing/* (all of them)
- app/globals.css (the design system: @theme tokens + component classes)

Deliver a STRUCTURED report with these parts:

PART A — PAGE INVENTORY. For each marketing page: its route, its purpose, the ordered list of sections/components it renders, and its approximate length/complexity. Note which pages share components and which reinvent their own layout (inconsistency = broken synergy).

PART B — COMPONENT INVENTORY. For each file in components/marketing/: one line on what it renders and where it's used. Flag components that are: (a) duplicative/overlapping, (b) unused/orphaned, (c) doing too much. Especially inventory the section primitives (sections.tsx, SectionHeading/FeatureCard/CtaBand, Reveal, cards) since these are the reuse layer.

PART C — DESIGN SYSTEM. Summarize app/globals.css: the color tokens (brand/navy/accent), the component classes (.card, .btn-*, .grad-text, .glass, etc.), animation keyframes, and the body background treatment. Note what's well-defined vs. what's ad-hoc/inline-styled across pages. This system's COLORS and ANIMATIONS are being KEPT — identify exactly what they are so a redesign can build on them.

PART D — CLUTTER DIAGNOSIS. Concretely: why does the homepage feel cluttered? Count the full-width stacked sections, note where visual weight is undifferentiated, where spacing rhythm breaks, where too much text/too many cards appear at once, and where hierarchy is flat. Be specific with section names and line references.

PART E — CURRENT INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE. The exact current nav structure (from MarketingHeader.tsx) and footer structure (MarketingFooter.tsx). Map every marketing route and whether it's reachable from nav/footer. Identify orphan pages and nav gaps.

PART F — BUILT-BUT-UNMARKETED FEATURES (very important). Cross-reference the actual platform capabilities against what the marketing site currently sells. Read prisma/schema.prisma and skim lib/actions*.ts to enumerate every real product/feature, then list which ones are NOT surfaced on the marketing site. Known candidates to verify: dedicated IPs, business email (EmailPlan/Mailbox), block-storage volumes (Volume), affiliate program, teams/organizations (Organization/Membership), server monitoring/alerts, gift codes, API tokens, 2FA, noVNC web console, automated backups + self-restore, game-server auto-update, one-click app/panel catalog, multi-node/region, Claude AI builder, coupons/referrals. For each, note whether it's marketed, partially marketed, or invisible — so the redesign can showcase everything we've built.

Keep it factual and cite file paths + line numbers. This report feeds the redesign's information architecture directly. Return the full report as your final message. Do not write code.
